text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- A new survey shows that one out of eight Danes is considering withdrawing money from bank accounts to invest in securities due to low interest rates on regular bank accounts.
--- Danish supermarket chains are very discontented with a recent rise in milk prices and dairies now fear that the supermarkets will turn to German dairies for cheaper milk.
--- Finance minister Mogens Lykketoft has rejected a demand from several social democratic mayors for a reintroduction of means testing to determine welfare benefits.
--- Denmark will probably not be able to participate in the military aspect of European Union operations in Zaire due to its Maastricht optouts on the West European Union, WEU.
--- Denmark's Chamber of Commerce estimates that the 1996 export boom, mainly created by companies in western Denmark, will continue in 1997 with growth of 5.7 percent compared to 5 percent in 1996.

--- Denmark's construction industry has gained a good foothold on the German market, sidelining German competitors on their own turf. Denmark exported building components to Germany worth 6.5 billion crowns in 1995, an increase of 400 million crowns compared to 1994.
